one_liner: NUMA-aware LD_PRELOAD malloc replacement, ~21% faster than glibc malloc and ~16% faster than mimalloc on 128-thread NUMA workloads.
what_it_does: Intercepts malloc/free/calloc/realloc (and pthread_create/join/kill) via LD_PRELOAD, giving each NUMA node its own heap tier and each thread its own per-thread heap on top, so multi-socket, multi-threaded C/C++ programs get NUMA-local memory without source changes. It targets large multi-socket servers -- the paper's machine has 8 nodes and 128 cores -- rather than single-socket desktops. There is no separate API: it's built as a single libnumalloc.so and swapped in as the process allocator.
how_it_is_fast: Layers a fast per-thread heap over a per-node heap tier, so the common malloc/free path never touches cross-node state; freed objects are returned to the heap tier matching the node they came from ('origin-aware' return) instead of a shared free list, keeping frees node-local under NUMA. During a program's single-threaded startup/teardown, an optional interleaved 'inter-heap' spreads allocations across all nodes to avoid one node absorbing all pre-fork memory. It's also built with transparent huge pages (-DUSE_HUGE_PAGE) to cut TLB misses on the large per-node heaps, which the ISMM'23 paper's own remote-access/TLB-miss profiling (perf) ties directly to the wins on dedup, fluidanimate, pbzip2, streamcluster and swaptions.
when_to_use: Multi-socket/multi-node NUMA Linux servers (paper: 8-node, 128-core Xeon Platinum 8153) running allocation-heavy, multi-threaded HPC or server workloads similar to PARSEC, CORAL-2 OpenMP/MPI, httpd, MySQL, or Memcached
You can rebuild the allocator with -DNUMA_NODES=<actual node count> -- it's hardcoded at compile time and the shipped Makefile defaults to 2
A plain C/C++ executable you can LD_PRELOAD, not something needing a vendored/linked allocator API
You can pin to an old toolchain matching the paper (GCC 8.3.0, C++14, Debian 10) and, critically, a pre-2.34 glibc
Research/reference use where you can independently validate results, not a production dependency
when_not_to_use: Any current Linux distro: an open, unmerged PR (#1, filed 2026-07-08) shows NUMAlloc infinite-recurses and crashes via an assertion the moment a second thread is created on glibc >= 2.34 (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, effectively any 2022+ distro), because its pthread_create interposition looks for a libpthread.so.0 that glibc merged into libc.so.6
Single-socket/single-NUMA-node machines -- the whole design is cross-node locality, so on one node you likely get the ~10-12% THP memory overhead for no throughput gain

Production or license-sensitive use -- no top-level LICENSE file; core NUMA-specific headers (pernodeheap.hh, perthreadheap.hh, interheap.hh) carry no license header at all, and files inherited from the FreeGuard project are GPL-2.0-or-later

Need active maintenance -- last push 2023-03-01, 2 GitHub stars, and the repo is a research dump of ~10 UTSASRG projects plus a dozen near-duplicate source-* variant folders with no indication which one produced the paper's numbers

Serial-phase-heavy programs -- the interleaved inter-heap exists specifically to offset interleaving costs during single-threaded phases, so a program that spends most of its time before spawning threads pays extra bookkeeping for little benefit

integration.dependencies: libnuma (-lnuma), pthread, librt, libdl -- all linked directly in source/Makefile
integration.min_toolchain: C++14 (Makefile CFLAGS); shipped Makefile builds with clang++, but the paper's numbers were built with GCC-8.3.0 -O2 -std=c++14 on Debian 10
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 only -- uses inline rdtscp asm and Linux's numa.h; NUMA_NODES is a compile-time #define that must be set to match the target machine's actual node count
integration.thread_safety: Not documented beyond source comments; relies on per-thread heaps for the fast path with locking in the shared per-node/global tiers, and the pthread_create/join/kill interposition itself is currently broken (infinite recursion) on any glibc >= 2.34 system per open PR #1
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial -- explain: LD_PRELOAD replaces malloc/free/calloc/realloc transparently with zero source changes, but it also interposes pthread_create/join/kill, and that interposition unconditionally crashes multi-threaded programs on glibc >= 2.34 as of this writing, so it is only a working drop-in on older glibc

gotchas: Open, unmerged PR #1 (2026-07-08): pthread_create resolves to the library's own wrapper instead of the real symbol on glibc >= 2.34, causing infinite self-recursion and an assertion crash on the second thread spawned under LD_PRELOAD; the author confirms the same bug exists in all ~12 source-* copies in the repo
NUMA_NODES is a compile-time constant (Makefile default 2, paper implies 8) -- building for the wrong node count is a silent topology mismatch, not a runtime-detected error
Heap is placed at a fixed virtual address (0x100000000000) rather than obtained from mmap(NULL, ...), which can collide with sanitizers or other tools that reserve that address range
About 10-12% higher RSS than glibc from transparent-huge-page use; drops to roughly glibc-comparable memory use with THP disabled (dropping -DUSE_HUGE_PAGE), per the input record's tradeoffs
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick NUMAlloc over SuperMalloc/Hoard/scalloc/rpmalloc/ltalloc/smmalloc only if you specifically need NUMA-node-local allocation on an 8-node-class multi-socket server, can rebuild for your topology, and are willing to fix the glibc>=2.34 pthread_create crash yourself; those siblings target single-node thread-count scaling and work off the shelf today, whereas NUMAlloc is an abandoned research prototype that currently fails to launch multi-threaded programs on modern Linux.
verified_claims_summary: Per the ISMM'23 manuscript (source/ISMM2023/evaluation.tex, read directly): on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8153 (8 nodes x 16 cores, 512GB RAM, Debian 10, GCC-8.3.0, THP+AutoNUMA on, hyperthreading off), averaged over 30 runs at 128 threads across PARSEC, five CORAL-2 OpenMP/MPI apps, and 7 real applications, NUMAlloc was 20.9% faster than glibc-2.28's default malloc and 15.7% faster than the next-best allocator tested (mimalloc-1.6.7), also beating TCMalloc, TCMalloc-NUMA, and TBB by 18-21%; the OpenMP/MPI subset alone showed 26.1% over glibc and 16.5% over mimalloc; best case fluidanimate was 5.3x glibc and 4.6x mimalloc. A superseded SC'22 draft in the same repo reports different numbers (19.0% vs glibc) for an overlapping but not identical benchmark set.
status_note: Abandoned since its last push on 2023-03-01 (2 GitHub stars) and usability is 'reference' only -- no top-level LICENSE, several core headers unlicensed, GPL-2.0-or-later on FreeGuard-derived files, and an unresolved crash-on-second-thread bug on any glibc >= 2.34 system as of this writing.
